_comment: What an innkeeper lets slip over an ale. Authored, never generated: host/npcd.py draws one at random for the ALE request. 'stages' limits a hint to those quest stages (see STAGES in host/npcd.py); 'inns' to those inn ids from assets/towns.txt. Each line must fit the C64's reply box (150 characters, plain ASCII) and must be true -- directions are the measured ones from assets/geography.json.

hints.text: The king's rider asked after you by name. Castle Matheson is south, where the land narrows. Do not keep a king waiting.
The castle is south of here, but the road bends a long way round. Mistress Coyle will sell you draughts for it.
The Hollow Crown is the deep place nearest the castle, in the south. That Sigil of yours is what opens it.
Vane will want more than a stone for his key. The fishers have a word for when the Drowned Stair runs dry. Ask one of them.
Old Brann has fished this water forty years. Ask him about the tide, and listen to how he says it.
The Drowned Stair is south-west of here, about 13 leagues on foot. Mind the hour.
The Drowned Stair lies west of Millford, near the northern shore. Wardlow folk know it better than we do.
Mother Ash in Ashcombe keeps the Ashen Key. Take her what you brought up out of the Stair.
Blackpit is in the deep forest to the south-west. The forest is thick with things that bite. Carry draughts.
Three stones, and Garrett the smith has the only anvil east of the Sundering fit to use them. He is in Millford.
Maldrath lairs high in the Sundering, in a burnt hollow on the western face. Go well rested.
Everyone is drinking to you tonight. You are still paying for your own, mind.
Keep to open grass where you can. Forest and swamp are where the beasts are thickest.
Drink a draught before a fight, not only in one. Mistress Coyle in Millford sells them.
The bowyer in Ashcombe sells bows. Shoot a beast before it reaches you and it has less to hit you with.
Garrett's forge in Millford sells blades, and the King's Armoury in Stonereach sells armour. Both are cheaper than a burial.
Whoever falls out there gets carried home to Millford, and wakes with half their purse gone.
The keepers of the deep places will not let you run. Go down ready, or do not go down.
Old Tam will tell you about the second army if you let him. He is the part of it that came back.
Salt, fish and books, that is Wardlow. Vane's library is the last one in Keldmarch, and he will tell you so.
